documents.title: Statement on Responsible and Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence

documents.title: Graduate Degree Requirements, Department of Computer Science, 2025
documents.stance_why: The handbook says generative AI to improve writing 'is not forbidden a priori', with limits set per class and a required pre-AI draft for the WCP, so AI is allowed under conditions.
documents.summary: The 2025 CS graduate handbook gives two short AI rules: the academic-integrity standard (AI for grammar and fluency is allowed but classes may restrict it) and the written critical review rule (keep a pre-AI draft). Graduate students only.

units.why: Part of the 'Non-original work' integrity standard: students 'must' submit their own work, which is P29 (own what you submit), must.
units.anchor: All work the students submit must be their own.

units.why: Permits generative AI for improving writing ('grammar, fluency'): P91, may. It is a permission, not just a prose-vs-code rule (P18).
units.anchor: The use of generative AI to improve writing (grammar, fluency), is not forbidden a priori

units.why: Says classes or degree requirements can restrict AI use further: per-class rules (P04); degree requirements are not instructors, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: may be further restricted in specific classes or specific requirement for the degree
units.fit_note: Also covers degree requirements, not only instructors.

units.why: Makes the student responsible for accuracy and plagiarism when using AI: ownership (P29), must. Accuracy part also touches P31 but the sentence assigns responsibility.
units.anchor: The student is responsible for accuracy and to avoid plagiarism.
units.fit_note: Includes responsibility for accuracy of AI-assisted writing.

units.why: In the written critical review (WCP) rules, generative AI for writing improvement is 'not forbidden': P91, may.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI to improve the writing (grammar, fluency) is not

units.why: WCP rule again makes the student responsible for accuracy and plagiarism: P29, must.
units.anchor: the student is responsible for accuracy and to avoid plagiarism
units.fit_note: Includes responsibility for accuracy of AI-assisted writing.

units.why: Requires an initial draft made before AI be available to the committee: sequencing, work first then AI (P90). P26 (submit drafts) fits less, since the point is the pre-AI state.
units.anchor: draft prior to AI use must be available for review by the committee.

documents.title: Graduate Degree Requirements, Department of Computer Science, 2023
documents.stance_why: The handbook says students 'should not use ... AI software for writing ... or any AI tools for content generation ... unless explicitly allowed to do so', a default ban with an exception.
documents.summary: The 2023 CS graduate handbook bans paraphrasing and AI writing or content-generation tools unless explicitly allowed, exempts spell-checkers, and tells students to ask if unsure. Probably replaced by the 2025 edition.
